 FIP1L1-PGDFRA GENE REARRANGEMENT 
Method – PCR		 NOT DETECTED     

Eosinophilia (eosinophils > 0.5 × 109/L) is a clinical finding that can be secondary to a large variety of diseases. When the evaluation of eosinophilia fails to reveal any underlying cause, Hypereosinophilic Syndrome (HES) is suspected. Chronic myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia and abnormalities of platelet-derived growth factor receptor-a(PDGFRA) had been referred to as chronic eosinophilic leukemia (CEL). Recently, the World Health Organization published new classification of tumors of hematopoietic and lymphoid tissues. According to this, eosinophilia is classified sub-typed into Chronic eosinophilic leukaemia, not otherwise specified (CEL-NOS) and Myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and abnormalities of PDGFRA, PDGFRB and FGFR1.

Chronic myeloid neoplasm (CMN) with abnormalities of PDGFRA is characterized by deletion on chromosome 4: del (4)(q12;q12), which accounts for the formation of a fusion gene consisting of the PDGFRA and FIP1L1 (FIP1-like-1) genes. The protein which is produced as a result of this chromosomal aberration has an increased tyrosine kinase activity, which causes neoplastic transformation of hematopoietic cells. The prevalence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene is about 10% to 15% of patients with chronic myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia and abnormalities of PDGFRA.
Eosinophil precursors release proinflammatory cytokines, mediators derived from arachidonic acid and enzymes toxic to surrounding tissues. Eosinophilic infiltration occurs in various organs leading to their damage. This causes a whole spectrum of accompanying symptoms, both general and related to pathologies of the cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, and gastrointestinal systems and to skin lesions.
Recently, studies have demonstrated that the prognosis of imatinib treated FIP1L1– PDGFRA-positive patients is outstanding and acquired resistance to imatinib is exceedingly rare.

Clinical Utility:

  1. Detection of the FIP1L1/PDGFRA fusion gene can also be used to predict response to Imatinib and to monitor therapeutic response in FIP1L1-PDGFRA-positive CMN with- eosinophilia patients.
  2. The presence of FIP1L1/PDGFRA fusion gene supports the diagnosis of chronic myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia with abnormalities of PDGFRA, PDGFRB and FGFR1 and rule out CEL-NOS.

Method: Nested RT-PCR
Interpretation:
The presence of an amplified product indicates the presence of FIP1L1/PDGFRA fusion gene.

Limitation:
The absence of the FIP1L1/PDGFRA fusion gene does not rule out the possibility of chronic myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia.
